subject.title: feat(gateway): idempotent start, non-interactive stop guard, unified lifecycle audit

question: Should `gateway stop` become fail-closed for every existing non-interactive caller, requiring `--force`, or should existing automation receive a compatibility/deprecation path?
rationale: This is a deliberate public CLI behavior change that can stop existing operational automation from functioning; code review cannot determine whether that compatibility break is an intended product policy.

options.title: Preserve automation compatibility
options.body: Keep the current non-interactive stop behavior or introduce a staged warning/deprecation path while retaining an explicit stricter mode for new automation.

options.title: Accept the fail-closed change
options.body: Require `--force` for all non-interactive stops, with clear upgrade guidance and direct proof of the refusal and recovery paths.

recommendation.title: Preserve automation compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep the current non-interactive stop behavior or introduce a staged warning/deprecation path while retaining an explicit stricter mode for new automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The assignee and author owns the proposed lifecycle policy and can clarify whether the compatibility break is intentional.
